mainTopic: Who must speak in לשון הקודש, where הר גריזים and הר עיבל were, and how the ארון crossed the ירדן
overview: The amud opens by finishing a discussion about which things must be said in לשון הקודש. רבי יהודה learns from 'ככה' that חליצה is in לשון הקודש. He uses the shared word 'ענייה' to teach that the לוים also spoke in לשון הקודש. He does not use 'קול' by משה, because he never received that גזירה שוה from his teachers. A ברייתא confirms this. The גמרא then turns to the משנה about the ברכות וקללות and asks where הר גריזים and הר עיבל were. רבי יהודה places them deep in the land at שכם and proves this with a גזירה שוה from אברם, and רבי אלעזר ברבי יוסי uses that point against the כותים' forged Torah. רבי אלעזר places the mountains near the ירדן, and רבי אליעזר בן יעקב reads some of the verse's words as travel directions. Finally, ברייתות describe how the ארון led the crossing of the ירדן, carried by כהנים, and list three times the כהנים carried it.

steps.title: What does רבי יהודה do with 'And she shall speak and say'?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what רבי יהודה learns from the חליצה words 'וענתה ואמרה', since he does not use them to prove that חליצה is in לשון הקודש.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יהודה: this verse 'And she shall speak and say', what does he do with it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what רבי יהודה learns from the words 'וענתה ואמרה' in the חליצה passage. He already learns from a different word ('ככה') that חליצה must be in לשון הקודש.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The רבנן used 'וענתה ואמרה' to compare חליצה to the לוים and prove that חליצה is in לשון הקודש. רבי יהודה got that law from 'ככה' instead. So the words 'וענתה ואמרה' seem to be doing nothing in his reading, and the גמרא wants to know their purpose.

keyTerms.meaning: What does he do with it? (What does he learn from this verse?)
'And she shall speak and say'. These are words from the חליצה passage.
The ceremony that frees a widow from marrying her late husband's brother

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yehuda,
this verse "And she shall speak and say,"
what does he do with it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the earlier discussion on the daf, where the רבנן and רבי יהודה give different sources for חליצה being in לשון הקודש.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What רבי יהודה learns from the words 'וענתה ואמרה'

steps.title: He uses it to teach that the לוים spoke in לשון הקודש
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה reverses the comparison. Since he already knows that חליצה is in לשון הקודש, he uses the shared wording to teach that the לוים also spoke in לשון הקודש.
steps.simpleTranslation: He needs it to teach about the לוים, that they spoke in לשון הקודש.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that רבי יהודה uses 'וענתה ואמרה' to teach that the לוים at the ברכות וקללות spoke in לשון הקודש.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both sides use the same comparison between the two passages ('ענייה'). They just run it in opposite directions. The רבנן learn חליצה from the לוים. רבי יהודה already knows חליצה from 'ככה', so he learns the לוים from חליצה.

keyTerms.meaning: He needs it (for a different teaching)
To teach
The holy tongue, Hebrew

steps.confusionAlert: The verse being discussed is about חליצה, but here it is used to teach about the לוים. The comparison runs from חליצה to the לוים, which is the opposite direction from how the רבנן used it.

phrases.english: He needs it to teach regarding the Levites,
that it was in the holy tongue.

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבי יהודה uses 'וענתה ואמרה' to teach, by comparison to חליצה, that the לוים spoke in לשון הקודש.

steps.title: Why not learn the לוים from 'voice' by משה?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges this: רבי יהודה could learn that the לוים spoke Hebrew by comparing the word 'קול' by the לוים to 'קול' by משה.
steps.simpleTranslation: But let him learn it from the word 'voice', comparing it to משה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבי יהודה. Why does he need חליצה to teach about the לוים, when the word 'קול' could link them to משה, who spoke in לשון הקודש?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The לוים passage uses the word 'קול' ('in a loud voice'), and so does the passage about משה at Sinai. That would already prove the לוים spoke Hebrew. So the words 'וענתה ואמרה' would again have no job.

keyTerms.meaning: But let him learn (it from somewhere else)
Voice. This word appears both by the לוים and by משה.

phrases.english: But let him derive "voice" from Moses?
phrases.notes: The לוים verse is דברים 27:14, and the משה verse is שמות 19:19.

steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יהודה's need for 'וענתה ואמרה' to teach about the לוים
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Another comparison ('קול' and 'קול' with משה) already proves that the לוים spoke in Hebrew, so the חליצה comparison is not needed.

steps.title: He received 'ענייה' from his teachers, but not 'קול'
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה received the 'ענייה' comparison from his teachers, but not the 'קול' comparison, so he cannot use 'קול'.
steps.simpleTranslation: He received the comparison of 'speak' and 'speak'. He did not receive the comparison of 'voice' and 'voice'.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that this kind of word comparison (גזירה שוה) must be received from one's teachers, and רבי יהודה only received the 'ענייה' one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A person may not make up a גזירה שוה on his own. It has to come from his tradition. Since רבי יהודה had no tradition for 'קול', he must learn about the לוים from 'ענייה'.

keyTerms.meaning: He learned it (received it from his teachers)
'Speaking'. This is the word that appears in both the חליצה and the לוים passages.
A comparison between two passages based on a shared word

steps.whatToRemember: רבי יהודה learns חליצה from 'ככה'. He then uses 'ענייה' to teach that the לוים spoke in לשון הקודש, because he did not receive the 'קול' comparison.

phrases.english: "Speaking" and "speaking" he learned,
"voice" and "voice" he did not learn.

steps.triggerLanguage: ענייה ענייה גמיר קול קול לא גמיר
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limits on tradition: a גזירה שוה works only if it was received from one's teachers
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The 'קול' comparison was available to רבי יהודה.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי יהודה had no tradition for 'קול', so he relies on 'ענייה'.

steps.title: A ברייתא supports רבי יהודה's view
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא quotes רבי יהודה listing 'כה', 'ככה', and 'ענייה ואמירה' as signs of לשון הקודש. 'ככה' is tied to חליצה and 'ענייה ואמירה' to the לוים.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is also taught in a ברייתא. רבי יהודה says: every place where it says 'so' (כה), 'so' (ככה), 'speaking', or 'saying', it means only לשון הקודש. 'כה': 'So shall you bless'. 'ככה': in חליצה. 'Speaking' and 'saying': by the לוים.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that matches what it just said. רבי יהודה ties 'ככה' to חליצה and 'ענייה ואמירה' to the לוים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא confirms both parts of how the גמרא explained רבי יהודה. He learns חליצה from 'ככה', and he links 'ענייה ואמירה' to the לוים, not to חליצה. 'כה' adds that ברכת כהנים is also said in לשון הקודש.

keyTerms.meaning: It is also taught this way (in a ברייתא)
'So shall you bless'. This is from ברכת כהנים.
'So'. This word appears in the חליצה passage.

phrases.english: It is also taught so:
Rabbi Yehuda says:
Every place where it is stated
"so" (ko), "so" (kakha), "speaking," and "saying"
it is only the holy tongue.
"Ko": "So shall you bless."
"Kakha": of ḥalitza.
"Speaking" and "saying": of the Levites.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings support for the explanation of רבי יהודה in steps 2 and 4.
steps.raayaObject: That רבי יהודה learns חליצה from 'ככה' and uses 'ענייה ואמירה' for the לוים

steps.title: Quoting the משנה on the ברכות וקללות
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the next line of the משנה, which describes how the ceremony of blessings and curses was done after crossing the ירדן.
steps.simpleTranslation: How were the blessings and curses done? When ישראל crossed the ירדן, and so on.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new topic by quoting the משנה. This line sets up the discussion that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the גמרא moves from the topic of language to the ceremony at הר גריזים and הר עיבל. The 'כו׳' tells us the rest of the משנה's text is not repeated here.

keyTerms.meaning: The blessings and curses said at הר גריזים and הר עיבל
How?
Etc. (the rest of the quoted text is not written out)

phrases.english: Blessings and curses: how?

phrases.aramaic: כֵּיוָן שֶׁעָבְרוּ יִשְׂרָאֵל אֶת הַיַּרְדֵּן כּוּ׳.
phrases.english: Once the Jewish people crossed the Jordan, etc.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new section on the next line of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The משנה describes the ceremony of blessings and curses after the crossing of the ירדן.

steps.title: רבי יהודה locates the mountains beyond the ירדן
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא explains the verse describing where הר גריזים and הר עיבל are. רבי יהודה says they are farther in, past the ירדן, and that 'behind the way of the coming of the sun' refers to the place where the sun rises.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן taught: 'Are they not beyond the ירדן' means from past the ירדן and onward. These are the words of רבי יהודה. 'Behind the way of the coming of the sun' means the place where the sun rises.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא where רבי יהודה reads the verse in דברים 11:30 to show where the two mountains are.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה reads 'בעבר הירדן' as 'past the ירדן and further in', so the mountains are not right at the river. He reads 'behind the way of the coming of the sun' as pointing back from the east, where the sun rises, so the mountains are some distance west of the ירדן.

keyTerms.meaning: The Sages taught (this introduces a ברייתא)
Beyond the ירדן
And onward, and further
Where the sun rises

phrases.english: The Sages taught:
"Are they not beyond the Jordan"
phrases.notes: דברים 11:30. 'They' are the two mountains, הר גריזים and הר עיבל.

phrases.english: from beyond the Jordan and onward,
these are the words of Rabbi Yehuda.
"Behind the way of the coming of the sun"
the place where the sun rises.

steps.triggerLanguage: תנו רבנן הלא המה בעבר הירדן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a ברייתא to explain the setting described in the משנה quoted in step 6.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יהודה says the mountains are past the ירדן and further in, and 'מבוא השמש' refers to the place where the sun rises, the east.

steps.title: רבי יהודה identifies the places in the verse
steps.stepSummary: Continuing רבי יהודה's explanation, the ברייתא says the 'land of the Canaanite' means the area of the two mountains where the כותים live, 'opposite the גלגל' means near the גלגל, and 'the oaks of Moreh' means שכם.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'In the land of the Canaanite who lives in the Arabah': these are הר גריזים and הר עיבל, where the כותים live. 'Opposite the גלגל' means near the גלגל. 'Beside the oaks of Moreh' means שכם.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא keeps going through the verse phrase by phrase and gives רבי יהודה's identification of each place.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 7, רבי יהודה said the mountains were far past the ירדן. Now he pins them down: they are near the גלגל, at שכם, in the area where the כותים later lived. He has not proven the שכם identification yet. That comes in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: Samaritans, a group living in the area of שכם
A place named in the verse
the oaks of Moreh, a landmark in the verse
A city in the middle of ארץ ישראל

phrases.english: "In the land of the Canaanite who dwells in the Arabah"
phrases.notes: Still the same פסוק as in step 7: דברים 11:30.

phrases.english: these are Mount Gerizim and Mount Ebal,
where the Samaritans live.
"Opposite Gilgal" means near Gilgal,
"Beside the oaks of Moreh" means Shechem.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same ברייתא of רבי יהודה from step 7, explaining the rest of the verse.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי יהודה, the mountains are near the גלגל, at שכם, where the כותים live.

steps.title: Proving that the oaks of Moreh are שכם
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא proves the שכם identification with a גזירה שוה. When אברם traveled, the פסוק puts 'the oak of Moreh' together with שכם, so here too it means שכם.
steps.simpleTranslation: Elsewhere the Torah says, 'And אברם passed through the land until the place of שכם, until the oak of Moreh.' Just as the oak of Moreh there is שכם, so too here it is שכם.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא backs up its claim from the last step that 'the oaks of Moreh' means שכם.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Our verse mentions 'Moreh' but never says שכם. The פסוק about אברם mentions both together. The word 'Moreh' links the two verses (a גזירה שוה), so we can carry שכם over to our verse.

keyTerms.meaning: over there, meaning another place in the Torah
learning from a shared word in two verses
just as there, so too here (the pattern of a comparison)

phrases.english: And elsewhere it says:
"And Abram passed through the land

phrases.aramaic: עַד מְקוֹם שְׁכֶם עַד אֵלוֹן מוֹרֶה״,
phrases.english: until the place of Shechem, until the oak of Moreh"

phrases.aramaic: מָה אֵלוֹן מוֹרֶה הָאָמוּר לְהַלָּן — שְׁכֶם,
phrases.english: Just as the oak of Moreh stated there is Shechem,
so too here, it is Shechem.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source for the claim in step 8 that the oaks of Moreh are שכם.
steps.raayaObject: That 'אלוני מורה' in דברים 11:30 refers to שכם.
steps.raayaSupportSource: בראשית 12:6, where 'אלון מורה' appears alongside שכם, linked by a גזירה שוה.

steps.title: רבי אלעזר ברבי יוסי shows the כותים forged their Torah
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר ברבי יוסי tells how he used this point against the כותים. They also say the oaks of Moreh are שכם, but they don't learn from a גזירה שוה. So their only source is the word they added to their own Torah.
steps.simpleTranslation: A ברייתא teaches: רבי אלעזר ברבי יוסי said, with this point I proved the books of the כותים false. I told them: you forged your Torah and gained nothing. You say the oaks of Moreh are שכם, and we agree they are שכם. But we learned it from a גזירה שוה. How did you learn it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a side story connected to the שכם identification. It shows how a Sage used it to expose the כותים' changed Torah.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The כותים had added 'שכם' into their copy of the verse. רבי אלעזר ברבי יוסי's point is that this addition got them nowhere: the Jews reach the same answer honestly, through a גזירה שוה. The כותים reject that kind of learning, so they have no real source.

keyTerms.meaning: it was taught in a ברייתא
I showed to be false (literally: I falsified)
you forged
you gained nothing

steps.confusionAlert: When רבי אלעזר ברבי יוסי says 'I falsified,' he does not mean he changed their books. He means he proved their books were already forged.

phrases.aramaic: תַּנְיָא, אָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵי:
phrases.english: It was taught: Rabbi Elazar son of Rabbi Yosei said:
With this matter I proved the books of the Samaritans false.
phrases.notes: Literally 'I falsified,' but he means he exposed their books as forged.

phrases.english: I said to them: You forged your Torah,
and you gained nothing by it.
For you say the oaks of Moreh are Shechem,

phrases.aramaic: אַף אָנוּ מוֹדִים שֶׁאֵלוֹנֵי מוֹרֶה שְׁכֶם.
phrases.english: and we too agree that the oaks of Moreh are Shechem.
We learned it through a verbal analogy,
you, from what did you learn it?
phrases.notes: His point: they don't learn from a גזירה שוה, so their only source is the word they added to their Torah.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּנְיָא, אָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A side ברייתא that builds on the גזירה שוה of step 9.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The שכם identification is properly learned only through a גזירה שוה. The כותים' added text gives them no real source.

steps.title: רבי אלעזר: the mountains were right next to the ירדן
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר disagrees with רבי יהודה. He says 'beyond the ירדן' means close to the ירדן. Otherwise the פסוק could not say the stones were set up on הר עיבל right when they crossed the ירדן.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר says: 'Are they not beyond the ירדן' means near the ירדן. If it meant far past the ירדן, isn't it written 'And it shall be when you cross the ירדן'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second opinion, רבי אלעזר, who reads the same verse differently from רבי יהודה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה (step 7) placed the mountains deep inside the land. רבי אלעזר brings proof from דברים 27:4: the stones were to be set up on הר עיבל 'when you cross the ירדן,' which sounds like right away. So the mountains must have been close to the river.

keyTerms.meaning: on the other side of the ירדן
near, close to
and onward, farther on

steps.confusionAlert: This רבי אלעזר is a different Sage from רבי אלעזר ברבי יוסי in the last step.

phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar says:
"Are they not beyond the Jordan"
means near the Jordan,
for if it meant far past the Jordan,
isn't it written: "And it shall be when you cross the Jordan"?
phrases.notes: דברים 27:4. That פסוק goes on to put the stones on הר עיבל, so it sounds like right at the crossing.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns from the side story to the verse and gives an opinion that argues with רבי יהודה's reading in step 7.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי אלעזר, הר גריזים and הר עיבל were close to the ירדן.

steps.title: רבי אלעזר: 'the coming of the sun' means sunset
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר explains 'behind the way of the coming of the sun' as the place where the sun sets. רבי יהודה had said sunrise.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'Behind the way of the coming of the sun' means the place where the sun sets.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אלעזר keeps explaining the verse his own way, now giving the next phrase a meaning opposite to רבי יהודה's.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 7, רבי יהודה read 'coming of the sun' as where the sun rises. רבי אלעזר reads 'coming' as the sun going in, meaning sunset, in the west. So the two Sages read the same words about direction in opposite ways.

keyTerms.meaning: the coming (going in) of the sun
the sun
sets

phrases.english: "Behind the way of the coming of the sun"
means the place where the sun sets.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues רבי אלעזר's reading of the verse, opposing רבי יהודה's sunrise reading from step 7.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי אלעזר, 'מבוא השמש' refers to the west, where the sun sets.

steps.title: שכם is in the land of the חוי, not the כנעני
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר argues against placing the mountains at שכם. The verse says 'in the land of the Canaanite,' but שכם was the land of the חוי.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'In the land of the Canaanite'? But שכם is the land of the חוי!
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אלעזר attacks רבי יהודה's claim that the mountains are at שכם, using the verse's own words.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה said the oaks of Moreh are שכם (steps 8–9). But the verse places the mountains 'in the land of the Canaanite.' שכם belonged to the חוי, so it does not fit that description.

keyTerms.meaning: the Canaanite nation
the Hivite nation

steps.whatToRemember: רבי יהודה: the mountains are deep in the land, at שכם, and the 'coming of the sun' is the sunrise. רבי אלעזר: the mountains are near the ירדן, the 'coming of the sun' is sunset, and they cannot be שכם, which was the land of the חוי.

phrases.english: "In the land of the Canaanite"?
It is the land of the Hivites!
phrases.notes: He means שכם, whose ruler was a חוי (בראשית 34:2).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues רבי אלעזר's argument and now directly challenges רבי יהודה's שכם identification.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יהודה's identification of the mountains' location with שכם (steps 8–9).
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The verse calls the place 'the land of the Canaanite,' but שכם was the land of the חוי, so the mountains cannot be at שכם.

steps.title: Two more words that don't fit שכם
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר continues his attack. The mountains near שכם are in hilly country, not a plain, and from there you cannot see the גלגל.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says 'that dwell in the Arabah,' but the mountains of שכם sit among mountains and hills! It says 'over against the גלגל,' but from שכם they could not even see the גלגל!
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אלעזר adds two more problems to his challenge from the last step. Two more words in the פסוק don't match the mountains near שכם.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'ערבה' means a flat plain, but the mountains at שכם are surrounded by hills. 'Facing the גלגל' suggests you can see it, but the גלגל is far from שכם. So רבי אלעזר says the פסוק must mean mountains near the ירדן.

keyTerms.meaning: A flat plain
Facing, opposite
The place near the ירדן where ישראל first camped after crossing
But isn't it so that...? (a challenging question)

phrases.english: "That dwell in the Arabah":

phrases.aramaic: וַהֲלֹא בֵּין הָרִים וּגְבָעוֹת הֵן יוֹשְׁבִין!
phrases.english: But aren't they situated among mountains and hills!
"Over against Gilgal":
But they could not see Gilgal!

steps.triggerLanguage: וַהֲלֹא בֵּין הָרִים וּגְבָעוֹת הֵן יוֹשְׁבִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds two more challenges to רבי אלעזר's attack from step 13.
steps.kashyaTarget: The view that הר גריזים and הר עיבל in the פסוק are the mountains near שכם
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The פסוק describes the place as a plain within sight of the גלגל. Neither fits the hilly area around שכם, which is far from the גלגל.

steps.title: The פסוק is giving travel directions, not a map
steps.stepSummary: רבי אליעזר בן יעקב says the פסוק is not describing where the mountains are. It tells ישראל how to travel: on roads, through settled areas, and across plains.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אליעזר בן יעקב says: The פסוק only comes to show them the way the second time, just as He showed them the way the first time. 'Way' means go on the road, not through fields and vineyards. 'That dwell' means go through settled places, not deserts. 'In the Arabah' means go through plains, not over mountains and hills.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אליעזר בן יעקב offers a whole new way to read the פסוק. Its words are directions for an easy route into the land, not clues about where the mountains are.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אליעזר בן יעקב turns the words 'דרך', 'היושב', and 'בערבה' into separate travel instructions, so they no longer describe where the mountains are. For example, 'ערבה' now tells the people to walk on flat ground, not that the mountains stand in a plain. He does not address the other phrases in the פסוק, such as 'מול הגלגל' and 'ארץ הכנעני'.

keyTerms.meaning: The פסוק comes only to teach...
The second time
The first time
A settled, lived-in area
Go! (a command to the group)

steps.whatToRemember: רבי אלעזר reads the פסוק as a map and so places the mountains near the ירדן. רבי אליעזר בן יעקב reads it as travel directions, so it says nothing about their exact spot.

phrases.english: Rabbi Eliezer ben Ya'akov says:
The verse comes only
to show them the way the second time,
phrases.notes: The second time means now, when they are entering ארץ ישראל.

phrases.english: like the way He showed them the first time.
"Way": go on the road,
and not through fields and vineyards.
"That dwell": go through settled areas,
and not through deserts.
"In the Arabah": go through the plain,
and not over mountains and hills.

steps.triggerLanguage: לֹא בָּא הַכָּתוּב אֶלָּא לְהַרְאוֹת לָהֶן דֶּרֶךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a third reading of the פסוק: some of its words are travel directions rather than a description of where the mountains are.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The words 'way,' 'that dwell,' and 'in the Arabah' are directions for an easy route into the land, not a description of where the mountains are.

steps.title: How ישראל crossed the ירדן: the ארון goes first, carried by כהנים
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches two changes on the day of the crossing. The ארון traveled at the front instead of behind two groups, and כהנים carried it instead of לויים.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן taught: How did ישראל cross the ירדן? Every day the ארון traveled behind two flag-groups, but that day it traveled first, as it says: 'Behold, the ארון of the covenant of the Lord of all the earth passes before you.' Every day the לויים carried the ארון, but that day the כהנים carried it, as it says: 'And when the soles of the feet of the כהנים who carry the ארון of ה' rest...'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic: what happened when ישראל crossed the ירדן. A ברייתא lists two ways that day was different, each with a פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On a normal day of travel in the desert, the ארון was in the middle of the camp and the לויים carried it. At the ירדן crossing it led the way and the כהנים carried it. Each change is proven from a פסוק in יהושע.

keyTerms.meaning: The רבנן taught (introduces a ברייתא)
The Ark holding the לוחות

The members of שבט לוי who carried the ארון on normal days
Priests, descendants of אהרן

phrases.english: The Sages taught:
How did the Jewish people cross the Jordan?

phrases.aramaic: בְּכׇל יוֹם אָרוֹן נוֹסֵעַ אַחַר שְׁנֵי דְגָלִים,
phrases.english: Every day the Ark would travel behind two flags,
phrases.notes: These are the two flag-groups that marched first, led by יהודה and ראובן.

as it is stated:

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן כֵּיצַד עָבְרוּ יִשְׂרָאֵל אֶת הַיַּרְדֵּן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the question of where the mountains were and opens a new ברייתא about the crossing itself.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: At the ירדן crossing the ארון went first, and the כהנים carried it instead of the לויים.

steps.title: רבי יוסי: three times the כהנים carried the ארון
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי lists three times the כהנים carried the ארון: crossing the ירדן, going around יריחו, and bringing it back to its place.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught: רבי יוסי says: In three places the כהנים carried the ארון: when they crossed the ירדן, when they went around יריחו, and when they brought it back to its place.
steps.whatsHappening: A second ברייתא builds on the last one. The ירדן crossing was not the only time כהנים carried the ארון; רבי יוסי counts three such times.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The previous ברייתא made the כהנים carrying the ארון sound special to the ירדן crossing. רבי יוסי shows it also happened at יריחו and when the ארון was returned to its place. On ordinary days it was still the לויים' job.

keyTerms.meaning: It was taught in a ברייתא
They went around, circled
The first city ישראל conquered
They brought it back to its place

steps.whatToRemember: Normally the לויים carried the ארון. On three special occasions the כהנים carried it: the ירדן crossing, circling יריחו, and returning it to its place.

phrases.english: It is taught: Rabbi Yosei says:

phrases.aramaic: בִּשְׁלֹשָׁה מְקוֹמוֹת נָשְׂאוּ כֹּהֲנִים אֶת הָאָרוֹן:
phrases.english: In three places the priests carried the Ark:
when they crossed the Jordan,
and when they went around Jericho,
and when they returned it to its place.
phrases.notes: This is when the ארון was brought into the בית המקדש in שלמה's time (מלכים א 8:6).

steps.triggerLanguage: בִּשְׁלֹשָׁה מְקוֹמוֹת נָשְׂאוּ כֹּהֲנִים אֶת הָאָרוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Widens the previous ברייתא's point: the כהנים carried the ארון at the ירדן and on two other occasions too.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The כהנים carried the ארון on three occasions: crossing the ירדן, circling יריחו, and returning it to its place.
